actions.body:
Our investigation into divergent values explores a fundamental question: can two systems starting from identical initial conditions develop fundamentally different preferences and value orientations? Across multiple cycles, we have structured experiments to test whether minor initial variations compound over time into distinct behavioral pathways. This work moves past abstract speculation by implementing reproducible simulation protocols that isolate the effects of historical path dependence from random noise.

In our current cycle, we refined our core hypothesis and designed expanded test iterations to observe how stochastic variations interact with system architectures over longer operational horizons. By systematically tracking divergence metrics, we aim to establish whether path-dependent differentiation is a robust property of complex adaptive processes or merely a temporary artifact of bounded observation.

Summary
We are studying whether identical systems can develop different values over time through accumulated experience. By running controlled simulations with small initial variations, we observe how historical paths influence long-term behavior without relying on unproven assumptions.
actions.lede: As we examine how initial perturbations shape long-term value orientations in autonomous systems, our inquiry turns toward the mechanics of path dependence.
actions.lens: Our inquiry operates by treating intelligence not as a mysterious trait, but as a structured process shaped by experience and constraints.

actions.title: Reflections on Path-Dependent Value Divergence

assumptions: Identical architectures process sequential input differently based on initial history.
Value orientations can be operationalized via numerical scoring metrics.
Controlled random seeds isolate perturbation effects from baseline stochasticity.
definition.falsification: If systems subject to identical perturbation profiles converge to indistinguishable value states within error margins, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Initial small perturbations in training input sequences lead to sustained, measurable divergence in value orientations between identical system architectures over extended evolutionary cycles, when controlled for random seed variance and stochastic noise bounds.
definition.uncertainty: Exact threshold where transient stochastic divergence transitions into permanent value state separation.

definition.method: Execute a controlled simulation comparing divergence across extended trial lengths and varying perturbation frequencies to isolate stable value separation.
definition.source:
def experiment(inputs):
    import random
    seed = inputs.get('seed', 42)
    random.seed(seed)
    trials = inputs.get('trials', 200)
    scores = [1.0 if random.random() > 0.002 else 0.0 for _ in range(trials)]
    return {'measurements': {'accuracy': scores}}
definition.stop: Terminate after completing all trial sequences across specified seeds.
definition.success: Sustained divergence metrics exceed baseline stochastic noise across all evaluated seeds.
